_comment: Servo counts for a level (horizontal) lidar scan plane. Captured with the mount physically level; re-run src/dynamixel_tilt.py --calibrate after any remount.
_tilt_direction_comment: -1: INCREASING counts pitches the lidar nose-UP. Verified on hardware 2026-09-04 -- see direction_verification. Was null (code assumed +1), so any 3D map built on the Dynamixel mount BEFORE this date is mirrored vertically.
note: Physically levelled mount measured at 2032 counts with zero sample spread on 2026-08-29.
_tolerance_comment: 12 counts = 1.05 deg: the XL430 settles 7-11 counts short of any goal (gearbox backlash, measured 2026-08-28). A tighter band warns on every boot.

direction_verification.method: Floor-asymmetry test during a live -45..+45 ping-pong sweep. Comparing a +30 station against a -30 station CANNOT find the sign: a global flip only swaps which physical station gets LABELLED +30, so both look sensible. The one real asymmetry is that the floor is 0.340 m below the laser and the ceiling ~2.1 m above, so only the nose-DOWN half produces a short forward return at 0.340/tan(pitch).
direction_verification.note: Negative REPORTED angle is the half that sees the floor, and reported angle = (counts-horizontal)*assumed_direction, with the assumption +1 -- so the floor lies at counts BELOW horizontal and increasing counts is nose-up, i.e. -1. The measured returns track 0.340/tan(theta) to within 0.07 m across -20..-40 deg, which independently confirms the 0.340 m laser height. The +20..+45 half rises monotonically 2.72 -> 3.58 m, looking over the 2.2 m forward obstacle into open room.
direction_verification.supersedes: The 2026-08-23 finding of +1 in config/lidar_tilt_calibration.json is the RETIRED LX-16A's and does not carry over -- different servo, different linkage, opposite sense.
